by.claim: Impersonation is rolled out per-project with no runbook connecting it to the diff path's permission model: when a CI diff job fails after impersonation is enabled on a project, the failure surfaces only as a Kubernetes RBAC error naming a service account, and the reporter chases the (broad) cluster Secret credential instead of the (narrow) destination service account the diff actually runs as, because the root cause — that diff always runs as the destination SA and may lack patch on cluster-scoped resources — exists only as an ad hoc note from a sync call, not as documented operator guidance.

Server-Side Diff on external clusters does not honor AppProject destinationServiceAccounts the way sync does, so each new resource kind in a chart forces another unbounded `patch` RBAC grant onto the narrow cluster credential just to compute a diff (RBAC has no dry-run verb); the observable failure mode is the Application status flapping Synced/Unknown on every reconcile, and there is no owner positioned to close the gap since the fix requires the diff path to adopt the same impersonation config the sync path already uses.

Once hydrated-commit signing is enabled, a rollback that pushes to a SourceIntegrity-protected branch outside the commit server lands unsigned and gets rejected by the git host, but the History & Rollback UI just shows a failed push with no messaging tying it to signing and no retry path — the operator has to manually track down who owns the commit server's signing key config to unblock a rollback, which is exactly the moment an operator most needs a fast, self-service recovery path.
